text: Shortest one, six, and distributed one, diffs. And of course, six is shorter than diffs. So why do we call it? We call this a time intervals a priority ladder. Priority, why ladder? Because we go from the shortest one to the longest one, okay? But why priority ladder? Because in our WiFi MAC, we exploit these time intervals to establish a priority in accessing the channel. And I will provide an example, so do not worry, but let me just finish the definition. And we will use six as time during which we need to sense the channel as idle before transmitting a high priority packet. While instead we use diffs that is longer to sense the channel as idle before being able to transmit a lower priority one. Let me give an example so that it will be easier to understand. So remember what we said earlier. That is, we are using carrier sense.
